question: Top programme scored MAIT — is this a MAIT population?
answer: NO. MAIT-defining genes are absent: SLC4A10 0.5%, ZBTB16 2.1%, RORC 0.1%, TRAV1-2 1.9%. The MAIT module scored high only on KLRB1 (16.7%) and NCR3 (5.5%), which are shared with conventional effector cells — TEMRA CD8 has KLRB1 14.6%. The module is not MAIT-specific at this panel size.
what_it_is: NK-like / innate effector CD8. FCGR3A 34.7% (vs 0.1% in naive), KLRD1 71.3%, NKG7 98.5%, TRGC2 34.5% — the same profile as TEMRA CD8 (FCGR3A 35.9%, KLRD1 77.9%, NKG7 99.7%). Only 56% carry an alpha-beta TCR (480/860), consistent with a partly innate compartment.
low_CD8_explained: Yes. NK-like CD8 cells downregulate surface CD8; the CD8A protein of 4.38 with CD8A RNA in 57% of cells is the expected pattern, not contamination.
manuscript_action: Defensible as named. State that CD8 surface expression is reduced in this population and that ~44% lack a detectable alpha-beta TCR. Reviewer 2's major 5c (congenital CMV CD16+ effector CD8) is directly relevant — cite it.

question: ADT CD8A 1.70 vs cohort median 16.03, CD4 RNA in 11% — is this CD4 contamination?
answer: NOT straightforward contamination. At single-cell level: 226 cells CD8-only, 65 CD4-only, only 2 double-positive, and 315 of 608 (51.8%) express NEITHER CD4 nor CD8A/CD8B. A contaminating CD4 population would be CD4-positive, not double-negative.
what_it_is: Predominantly a double-negative-by-detection population. 489/608 (80%) carry an alpha-beta TCR, so they are T cells. No MAIT signature (SLC4A10 0.3%), no gamma-delta (TRDC 0%, TRGC1 0.3%), no NK programme (NKG7 6.9%, KLRD1 3.8%).
low_CD8_explained: Partly. Depth is mid-range (median 1,861 genes / 5,080 UMI) so this is not global dropout, but the dominant class is non-detection of BOTH lineage markers rather than positive CD4 signal. Protein CD8A of 1.70 means surface CD8 is genuinely low, not merely undetected in RNA.
manuscript_action: DO NOT present as a fourth naive CD8 subset without qualification. Options: (a) relabel to reflect low/absent surface CD8, (b) report it and state the ambiguity explicitly, (c) exclude from the naive-subset claim and report separately. This is a judgement call for the authors — it is 608 of 18,843 cells (3.2%) and is one of the four naive subsets in the abstract's first finding.
